issues.detail: Covers the happy path only: there is no handling for missing files, unsupported codecs, channel collisions, or failed renders, and the description's promised render-time estimation is never covered.

scenarios.name: crossfade-timeline-from-shot-list
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric closely (checks/creates the sequence editor, uses strips.new_movie, alternates channels 1/2, overlaps by 12 frames, and adds GAMMA_CROSS via new_effect with length/input1/input2 on channel 3), while A uses type CROSS, frame_end/seq1/seq2 as the primary kwargs, and a .sequences fallback, which the rubric explicitly excludes.

scenarios.name: audio-fade-and-text-overlay
scenarios.rationale: Both keyframe volume 0→target→0 and set text/color/font_size/location/anchor centering, but A uses strips.new_effect with length=72 and right_handle exactly as the rubric specifies, whereas B uses frame_end for the title (not length), frame_final_end for the end, and sets unverified align_x/align_y properties rather than alignment_x.

scenarios.name: render-mp4-h264-from-strips
scenarios.rationale: B meets nearly every rubric item (strips_all with left_handle/right_handle, MPEG4/H264/AAC, 1080p, render animation, blender --background --python), while A uses deprecated frame_final_start/frame_final_end and sequences_all, and passes the .blend with -b rather than the exact invocation, though otherwise setting format/codec correctly.
